title: Khayyam's Cubics and the Hidden Conic
summary: Omar Khayyam's treatment of cubic equations by intersections of conic sections has often been read as an anticipation of analytic or coordinate geometry. This paper argues that such a reading obscures the conceptual structure of Khayyam's own method. Working within the geometric framework of Euclid and Apollonius, it reconstructs Khayyam's thirteen cubic species through the local conic relations generated by his proportional arguments.
